MAJOR: fix_guard.enforced() checks is_closed() BEFORE the explicit config `enforce_items` list, so config-enforced items (BI-PF-1531/1508) silently escape enforcement when marked closed — fail-open against config/fix-impact.json contract.

fix_guard.problems() early-returns [] when no BLOCKER/MAJOR findings are present, so an absent/corrupt review artifact (latest_review -> {}) now passes where it previously reported 'fix_impact missing' — gate fails open on missing evidence.

Delta ships unrelated BI-PF-1531 tooling (scripts/dev/architect_review.py, fix_guard.py, review_select.py, test_fix_guard.py); none are in the design's declared affected_files and no BI-PF-1267 design/AC covers these changes.
MINOR: `required` and the later `req` list-comprehension in problems() are byte-identical; the second is dead duplication that will drift when severity filters change.
review_select still uses p.stat().st_mtime as the tie-break key, so records with equal or missing `at` remain checkout-order dependent; only a log line mitigates the original BI-PF-1531 flake.
is_closed() lazily imports core.backlog and calls backlog.section, coupling a pure selection helper to the backlog authority (env/DB side effects inside CI gates).

architect_review defers `from review_select import latest_review` to the call site instead of module-level import, hiding the dependency from static analysis and inconsistent with the rest of the file.
fix-guard --all/--item output gained a second summary line with different field order; strict parsers keyed on the single 'fix-guard: OK|FAIL' line may need updating.
NIT: `_J = "." + "json"` filename-construction workaround in test_fix_guard.py is opaque and fragile against future store-contract changes.
glob pattern f"{item_id}-*.json" does not escape glob metacharacters in item_id.
review_select is_closed duplicates the closed-status vocabulary in the test, so config/status changes require two edits.
SUMMARY: Delta is internally well-tested tooling refactor (shared deterministic selector is the right reuse), but it is out of BI-PF-1267 scope and weakens fix-guard into fail-open paths (closed-status short-circuit before enforce_items, empty-review early return).
AC-1 (contract parity) is unaffected by this delta; top risks are gate-integrity regressions in fix-guard and unreviewed scope creep.
